items.title: Gouvernement : Ramid plaide pour un ministère dédié aux Droits de l'Homme
items.description: Dans le cadre des tractations politiques intenses relatives à la constitution du futur gouvernement conduit par la Cheffe du gouvernement désignée, Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, l'ancien ministre de la Justice et des Libertés, Mustapha Ramid, a livré une analyse sans détour sur l'état des libertés et l'équilibre institutionnel au Maroc. À travers une prise de parole publique, l'ancien dirigeant politique estime que le Royaume, se situant dans une zone intermédiaire entre modèle démocratique accompli et autoritarisme, doit intensifier ses efforts officiels et civils pour parfaire sa transition vers une démocratie pleine et entière. L'ancien ministre dresse un constat critique à l'égard de l'écosystème institutionnel actuel, pointant du doigt ce qu'il qualifie de relâchement et de repli sur soi du Conseil National des Droits de l'Homme durant les dernières années. Selon lui, cette instance a progressivement délaissé son rôle d'action effective et de protection proactive des libertés individuelles et collectives. Parallèlement, Mustapha Ramid soulève les limites structurelles de la Délégation interministérielle aux Droits de l'Homme, dont les prérogatives restent cantonnées à la coordination technique entre départements pour la rédaction de rapports périodiques et l'interaction avec les mécanismes des Nations Unies, sans véritable pouvoir d'impulsion politique. Pour fonder sa proposition d'inclure un portefeuille ministériel dédié aux Droits de l'Homme dans la future équipe gouvernementale, Mustapha Ramid s'appuie sur une lecture stricte de l'article 92 de la Constitution. Ce texte stipule que le Conseil de gouvernement délibère obligatoirement des questions d'actualité et des textes relatifs aux droits de l'Homme et à l'ordre public. L'ancien ministre souligne l'asymétrie institutionnelle actuelle : alors que l'ordre public dispose d'un garant puissant et influent incarné par le ministre de l'Intérieur, les droits de l'Homme se retrouvent dépourvus d'un défenseur de rang ministériel capable de faire contrepoids lors des arbitrages exécutifs. Sans un ministre identifié portant spécifiquement la casquette des droits humains, ou combinant cette charge avec un portefeuille connexe comme la Justice, cette thématique risque d'être marginalisée au sein du Conseil de gouvernement et dans la conduite des politiques publiques. Les délibérations gouvernementales obéissant à une logique sectorielle où chaque ministre défend prioritairement son périmètre, l'absence d'un tutélaire dédié voue les enjeux de libertés à un isolement préjudiciable. Revenant sur les expériences gouvernementales passées, Mustapha Ramid qualifie d'erreur l'abandon de ce pôle ministériel lors de la constitution de précédentes moutures exécutives. Il rappelle à ce titre que la présence d'un ministre dédié avait permis d'imposer les principes de la démocratie et de l'État de droit au cœur de la déclaration gouvernementale. Même si ce portefeuille ne dispose pas toujours de leviers exécutifs directs face à la rigidité de certains départements régaliens, l'autorité morale et politique d'un tel ministre permet d'instaurer une vigilance constante et d'influencer positivement l'action publique globale. The post Gouvernement : Ramid plaide pour un ministère dédié aux Droits de l'Homme appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: AGI urges investment in skills and raw materials to strengthen local manufacturing
items.description: The Association of Ghana Industries (AGI) is stepping up efforts to strengthen Ghana’s garment, textiles and leather sector, following the government’s decision to engage local manufacturers to produce uniforms and other apparel for the security services. The initiative is expected to create opportunities for local businesses, but industry players say addressing skills shortages, high production costs, and limited access to raw materials will be critical to strengthening industry demand. Chairperson of AGI’s Garment, Textiles and Leather Sector, Edwina Assan, says the association is engaging training institutions and industry players to develop the skills needed to strengthen local production. She noted that some institutions lack the technical expertise and personnel to train workers for the industry, making collaboration with experienced manufacturers necessary. “We are looking at coming up with programmes that the industry players can help with, supporting the institutions in training,” she said. She also identified the high cost of imported raw materials and other production inputs as major constraints affecting local manufacturers. According to her, reducing dependence on imported materials through local production will help lower manufacturing costs and make Ghanaian products more competitive. “It’s only when we have our raw materials produced locally that we can also produce at a cheaper price and be able to pay well,” she added. Meanwhile, the Chief Executive Officer of Horseman Shoes, Tonyi Senayah, says Ghana must be deliberate in building the capacity of local footwear and leather businesses before considering restrictions on imported products. He questioned whether local companies currently have the production capacity to meet domestic demand, arguing that protecting the industry must go hand in hand with investment in skills, enterprise development, and market access. “What we are advocating for is that we start building the capacity of players or enterprises in the footwear and leather space. And we have to be intentional,” he said. Mr. Senayah noted that successful industrial economies developed their manufacturing sectors through deliberate policies and sustained support for local businesses. He believes the leather industry presents significant opportunities for job creation, particularly among young people, but says local enterprises need the right support to expand and compete. “By being intentional, we have to start building the capacity of these businesses, developing skills and also giving them access to market,” he added. The industry says stronger collaboration, improved technical training, and increased local raw material production will be essential to expanding Ghana’s manufacturing capacity. It believes these measures will help local businesses take advantage of government procurement opportunities, create employment, and strengthen the country’s garment, textiles and leather value chain.

items.title: 4 men killed in landmine explosion near LoC in Azad Kashmir
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Four men were killed on Monday when a landmine exploded near the Line of Control (LoC) in the Poonch district of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), according to the Directorate General of Public Relations (DGPR). The DGPR said in a statement, citing initial reports, that the four men were at the site of the incident in Hajira tehsil to repair a pipeline carrying spring water, when the landmine floated into the area from the Indian side and exploded. All four of them died on the spot, the statement said. It added that due to unclear border demarcation in areas close to the LoC, floating unexploded landmines posed a persistent threat to civilians and livestock. The DGPR statement had no further details of the incident. Earlier, Poonch Divisional Commissioner Sardar Waheed Khan said while speaking to Dawn that Indian Army personnel had planted the landmine. Former AJK prime minister Sardar Abdul Qayyum Niazi expressed grief over the deaths and offered condolences to the bereaved families. In a statement, he said India was killing Kashmiris — not only in the occupied territory but also along the LoC in Azad Kashmir — by planting improvised explosive devices and shooting people engaged in routine activities such as herding cattle, cutting fodder and collecting medicinal plants. He blamed the continued loss of lives on the prolonged delay in resolving the Kashmir issue, which he attributed to India’s reluctance.

items.title: Dr Fatma Guenoun, présidente de la Lisca: gardienne de l’espoir des femmes cancéreuses
items.description: Son sourire donne le ton. Dr Fatma Guenoun rit facilement, plaisante au détour d’une réponse et garde une pointe de malice dans une conversation consacrée à une maladie qui bouleverse tant de vies. Cette gaieté accompagne pourtant une histoire profondément liée à la souffrance des femmes qu’elle reçoit depuis des années dans les services de cancérologie. Au fil de son parcours, elle a rencontré des patientes pour lesquelles le diagnostic ouvrait aussi une bataille financière, avec des traitements difficiles à financer et des familles contraintes à de lourds sacrifices. Elle a choisi de porter leur cause, de chercher des soutiens et de faire entendre leur voix. Le cancer a fini par croiser son propre chemin avec la découverte d’une masse, les examens et la chirurgie, l’entraînant dans une vie de patiente qu’elle connaît de l’intérieur. Face à l’épreuve, son humour reste là, accompagné par la foi et par le soutien de ceux qui l’entourent. On remarque d’abord son sourire. Il accompagne sa voix, ses souvenirs et même les passages les plus lourds de son récit. Dr Fatma Guenoun parle de cancer avec les mots d’un médecin habitué aux consultations, aux diagnostics, aux traitements et aux inquiétudes des familles, mais son histoire personnelle donne à ses paroles une résonance particulière. Lorsqu’on lui demande qui est derrière la médecin et la présidente de la Ligue sénégalaise contre le cancer, elle répond en revenant à l’essentiel, à sa famille, à ses liens et à son engagement auprès des femmes fragiles. « C’est une femme. Une femme qui est mère de famille, qui est sœur, qui est tante, qui est grand-mère et qui est épouse. Je suis une femme aussi engagée dans les causes des femmes démunies ». La réponse dit beaucoup de celle qui dirige la Ligue sénégalaise contre le cancer (Lisca). La blouse blanche représente une partie de son parcours. La présidence de l’association en représente une autre. Au centre, il reste une femme attachée aux siens et attentive aux vies fragilisées par la maladie et par les difficultés financières. Son engagement prend racine à l’hôpital, car, elle y a rencontré des femmes venues chercher des soins avec leurs inquiétudes, leurs ordonnances et leurs moyens limités. Une consultation pouvait rapidement se transformer en épreuve économique. Une biopsie, un traitement, une séance de chimiothérapie pouvaient engager des sommes capables d’épuiser les économies d’une famille. Certaines vendaient leurs bijoux, des maris cédaient leurs voitures et des familles mettaient leurs maisons en vente pour tenter de financer les soins. « Le déclic, ça vient de l’hôpital. Je suis médecin dans un institut du cancer où je reçois des femmes, des femmes démunies », confie-t-elle. À partir de là, son engagement a pris une dimension plus large. Elle cherche des appuis, interpelle, mobilise et fait de la prise en charge des femmes atteintes de cancer une cause à porter collectivement. L’histoire de la Lisca garde notamment la trace d’un mois d’octobre 2014. L’association disposait alors de moins de 100.000 FCfa dans ses comptes pour lancer « Octobre Rose ». Des lettres sont envoyées, des rubans sont remis à la ministre de la Santé de l’époque, le professeur Awa Marie Coll Seck, avec l’espoir qu’ils arrivent jusqu’au Président Macky Sall. Le 1er octobre, lors du Conseil des ministres, le Président demande à chaque ministre de soutenir au moins cent femmes. La campagne a changé alors d’échelle et les soutiens ont afflué. Dr Fatma Guenoun raconte cet épisode avec la mémoire précise de celle qui a vécu le passage d’une association disposant de moyens dérisoires à une organisation capable de mobiliser autour d’une cause nationale. « Nous sommes partis de zéro franc et nous sommes arrivés à plusieurs millions avant la fin de la campagne », se rappelle-t-elle, guillerette. Le goût du combat Le cancer finit pourtant par entrer dans sa propre histoire. Elle découvre elle-même une masse au niveau du sein. En tant que médecin, elle connaît les étapes qui suivent. Mammographie, biopsie, résultats et puis discussion avec le chirurgien. Elle connaît aussi son terrain familial, marqué par plusieurs cas de cancer, notamment cinq cas de cancers. La décision est prise avec son chirurgien. « C’est moi-même qui ai diagnostiqué ma masse. J’ai fait la mammographie, la biopsie et j’ai eu les résultats. En accord avec mon chirurgien, nous avons décidé de faire une mastectomie parce que je suis un sujet à risque », nous confie-t-elle. Dans son récit, la découverte du cancer garde une place particulière. Elle parle de sérénité, avec la distance de celle qui a déjà connu plusieurs interventions chirurgicales pour des tumeurs bénignes et qui a appris à accueillir les épreuves médicales avec lucidité. Cette expérience personnelle nourrit aussi une réflexion sur le rapport aux femmes qu’elle accompagne à la Lisca. Son regard reste marqué par la même attention. Elle a toujours cherché à soutenir psychologiquement les patientes. Face à sa propre maladie, elle puise elle aussi dans les ressources qui permettent de tenir. La foi occupe une place importante dans son récit, avec le soutien de sa famille et de ses amis. « Je me soutiens moi-même grâce à la foi et au soutien de mon entourage, de ma famille et de mes amis ». Son combat garde aussi une dimension collective. Dans les couloirs de l’hôpital, dans les campagnes de dépistage et dans les échanges avec les malades, elle mesure les progrès accomplis et les difficultés qui demeurent. La prise en charge du cancer reste coûteuse et la couverture par la Couverture maladie universelle reste insuffisante. Certaines chimiothérapies conventionnelles bénéficient de dispositifs de gratuité et certains produits ont connu des réductions de prix. Battre le cancer à tout point de vue La question des ruptures de médicaments reste toutefois une source majeure de préoccupation. Elle évoque encore une ordonnance reçue le jour même de l’entretien. Un produit prescrit figure en rupture. Pour une personne qui commence son traitement, l’absence d’un médicament ne représente jamais une information anodine. Elle nourrit l’angoisse, fragilise le moral et fait naître des interrogations sur la continuité des soins. « Ce qui me révolte, ce sont les ruptures. Quand on commence un traitement et qu’un produit est en rupture, ça pose des problèmes psychologiques aux malades », explique Dr Guenoun. Elle connaît donc les deux côtés de la maladie. Celui de la médecin qui explique, oriente et accompagne et celui de la patiente qui reçoit un résultat, traverse une intervention et apprend à vivre avec une nouvelle réalité corporelle. Entre ces deux expériences, elle garde la conviction, celle d’une lutte qui mérite d’être menée avec courage et avec foi. Aux femmes qui viennent de recevoir un diagnostic, elle adresse un message qui ressemble à sa personnalité, direct, chaleureux et tourné vers l’espoir. « Il faut croire, avoir la foi et dire qu’on peut guérir. Avoir le cancer, c’est un combat, mais on peut gagner le combat », gage-t-elle. Elle revient enfin au dépistage, son autre bataille. Son appel s’adresse aux femmes, mais aussi à leur entourage. Elle demande aux hommes de pousser leurs épouses à faire consulter, aux enfants d’encourager leurs mères, aux cousins et aux oncles de rappeler aux femmes de leur famille l’importance du dépistage. « Moi, ce que je vais dire à toutes les femmes, c’est d’aller se faire dépister. Je dis aux époux, aux enfants, aux cousins, aux oncles d’inciter les femmes de leur entourage à aller se dépister ». Elle sourit encore lorsqu’elle parle. Le rire accompagne la gravité du sujet sans l’effacer. Fatma Guenoun continue avec sa foi, son humour et une conviction forgée au contact des malades, des familles et de sa propre histoire. Son combat pour les femmes porte désormais aussi la marque d’une expérience intime. Une expérience qui donne à sa voix une profondeur particulière lorsqu’elle parle de dépistage, de soins et d’espoir. Par Amadou KÉBÉ

items.title: GPL 2026/27: ‘We have to rectify our mistakes’ – Boadu reacts to Aduana FC defeat
items.description: Aduana FC head coach Samuel Boadu has urged his team to quickly put their latest defeat behind them and focus on correcting their errors ahead of upcoming Ghana Premier League fixtures. Aduana FC brought their three-match winning streak to an end following a 1-0 defeat over the Young Apostles at the Wenchi Sports Stadium. A first-half penalty converted by Samuel Prempeh shortly before the break proved decisive, securing all three points for the home side. “I don’t want to talk about officiating. It is football,” Boadu said. “We have lost, and we have to rectify our mistakes going into the remaining games. I wasn’t expecting a defeat, but one mistake we made resulted in their goal.” “It was really bad, but we will talk to ourselves and improve in subsequent games. I will congratulate my players despite the defeat. It was one unpardonable mistake that led to the loss.” Despite the setback, Boadu declined to set explicit targets for the remainder of the campaign. “It is still early days to talk about our target. We will go home, work hard, and aim to accumulate more points in our subsequent matches,” he explained. The result leaves Aduana FC sixth on the Ghana Premier League standings with 10 points after six matches.

items.title: No disability access, no building permit – KMA declares
items.description: The Chief Executive of the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA), Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi, has admitted that most public infrastructure in the metropolis, including his own office, is not disability-friendly. According to him, the challenge stems from the fact that most public buildings in the city were constructed before the passage of Ghana’s Disability Act and are housed in old institutional structures not designed with accessibility in mind. “Even my office and the entire KMA complex are not PWD-friendly, but these are old buildings and there is nothing we can do about them now. However, we will ensure that accessibility for PWDs is prioritized in any future infrastructure development or redevelopment on the KMA premises,” he said. Speaking to Adom News, Mr. Boadi stated that since he assumed office, he has ensured strict enforcement of the accessibility requirements stipulated in the Persons with Disability Act, 2006 (Act 715), for all new developments within the metropolis. “For every new building permit proposal that comes before us, we ensure that if it is going to serve the public, you must create ramps and channels that will ensure accessibility for our brothers and sisters with disabilities before we give approval,” he said. He disclosed that the Assembly has captured 18 projects in its 2027 development plan aimed at making public spaces more inclusive. The projects include the massive renovation of parks and community centres across the metropolis. The renovation, he explained, will involve the demolition and reconstruction of stages to incorporate appropriate ramps and accessible facilities to enable talented PWDs to access the platforms, showcase their talents and earn a living. “It is something the Assembly has not taken its eyes off. For example, the Prempeh Assembly Hall is not disability-friendly, so its renovation to make it accessible has been captured in our budget,” the Mayor assured. Mr. Boadi reaffirmed KMA’s commitment to promoting disability inclusion and ensuring that persons with disabilities participate fully in the social and economic life of the metropolis.

items.title: Top 10 African companies ranked among Forbes’ best employers in 2026
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye South Africa’s Nedbank has emerged as Africa’s highest-ranked company on Forbes’ World’s Best Employers 2026 list, placing 26th globally, while Nigeria’s Guaranty Trust Bank (GTBank) is the only Nigerian firm among the continent’s 10 highest-ranked entries. The ranking, compiled by Forbes in partnership with Statista, features 900 companies headquartered in 52 countries, following a survey of more than 300,000 employees across over 50 countries. Nine of Africa’s 10 highest-ranked companies are headquartered in South Africa, reflecting the country’s strong representation among large multinational employers. GTBank ranks 277th globally and 7th in Africa, ahead of South African energy and chemicals company Sasol, healthcare group Mediclinic International and financial services firm Sanlam. Here are the 10 highest-ranked African companies on Forbes’ World’s Best Employers 2026 list. Nedbank — 26th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Banking and financial services Nedbank is Africa’s highest-ranked company on the 2026 list, placing 26th globally. The South African banking group rose from 49th position in the 2025 edition, moving up 23 places to lead the continent’s entries. The latest position earned by Nedbank puts it ahead of other African banking groups, including Standard Bank Group, Absa Group and FirstRand. Standard Bank Group — 54th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Banking and financial services Standard Bank Group ranks second among African companies with the best employers and 54th globally. The bank fell from 28th position in 2025, dropping 26 places in the latest edition. Despite the decline, it remains one of Africa’s highest-ranked employers, alongside three other South African banking groups in the global top 105. Absa Group — 98th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Banking and financial services Absa Group ranks third among African companies and 98th worldwide. The South African financial services group recorded a slight decline from 97th position in the previous edition. Absa’s latest ranking significantly keeps it among the continent’s four highest-ranked employers, all of which are South African banking groups. FirstRand — 104th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Banking and financial services FirstRand ranks fourth among African companies and 104th globally. The financial services group is the parent company of banking brands including First National Bank and Rand Merchant Bank. MTN Group — 133rd globally Country: South Africa Sector: Telecommunications MTN Group ranks fifth among African companies and 133rd globally. The telecommunications company rose 33 places from its 166th position in 2025 and retained its position as the world’s third-highest-ranked telecommunications employer. MTN operates across multiple African markets, including Nigeria. Its ranking refers to the wider group rather than its Nigerian operations alone. Investec — 197th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Banking and financial services Investec ranks sixth among African companies and 197th globally. The international financial services group operates in banking, wealth management and investment services. Guaranty Trust Bank — 277th globally Country: Nigeria Sector: Banking and financial services Guaranty Trust Bank is the only Nigerian company among Africa’s 10 highest-ranked employers on the 2026 list. The commercial bank ranks 277th globally, making it the seventh-highest-ranked African entry and its latest position places it ahead of Sasol, Mediclinic International and Sanlam in the continental ranking. GTBank’s inclusion also gives Nigeria representation in a list otherwise dominated by South African companies. Sasol — 298th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Energy and chemicals Sasol ranks eighth among African companies and 298th globally. The South African energy and chemicals group operates across industries involving fuels and chemical products. Sealing a place in the global 300 is significant as it makes the Energy company one of the continent’s highest-ranked employers outside the banking and telecommunications sectors. Mediclinic International — 460th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Healthcare Mediclinic International ranks ninth among African companies and 460th worldwide. The healthcare group operates hospitals and provides specialist medical services. Sanlam — 470th globally Country: South Africa Sector: Insurance and financial services Sanlam completes the African top 10, ranking 470th globally. The South African financial services group has interests in insurance, investments, retirement savings and wealth management. Its placement makes it the 10th-highest-ranked African company in the 2026 list. items.title: Asantehene to lead environmental restoration effort at Jimi Land Reclamation Site
items.description: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, will undertake a royal visit to the Jimi Land Reclamation and River Watercourse Rehabilitation Project near Obuasi on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. During the visit, he will plant trees and inspect Lot 1, marking a major milestone in restoring lands severely degraded by unregulated small-scale mining. The environmental initiative responds to widespread damage caused by unregulated small-scale gold mining, known as galamsey, which has stripped forest vegetation, contaminated soils, and left hazardous open, water-filled pits across the Obuasi and Adansi areas. Toxic runoff and heavy sediment buildup along the Jimi River threaten the Jimi Dam, a critical source of drinking water for communities across the Adanse Traditional Area. The reclamation effort stems from Otumfuo’s advocacy against illegal mining during the Mining in Motion forum, which led to the creation of the Ashanti Green Initiative. Operating as the initiative’s flagship pilot project, the Jimi reclamation brings together key institutional partners, including the Manhyia Palace, providing overall strategic vision and royal patronage; Ashanti Green Initiative, serving as project lead on behalf of the Asantehene and drives community engagement; and AngloGold Ashanti, delivering technical and operational support. Others are the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, overseeing policy, permitting, and security enforcement through NAIMOS and the Blue Water Guard; and the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), providing regulatory guidance for ecological restoration along the river and buffer zones. Covering 153 hectares across three designated lots in the Obuasi East Municipality as well as the Adansi Akrofuom and Adansi Asokwa Districts, the pilot targets heavily impacted sites near Gyimisokakraba, Ayease, and Akwesi Ankromakrom. Restoration works are structured around a six-step process: Backfilling open mining pits and deep gullies; Re-grading spoil heaps and terracing steep slopes; Containing, capping, or removing heavy-metal soil contamination; Installing drainage and erosion control structures to safeguard the river corridor; Restoring and enriching topsoil health; and replanting the land with kenaf, a commercial fibre crop. Due to residual heavy-metal contamination risks in the soil, kenaf was selected over food crops. The fast-growing fibre crop will be harvested for manufacturing sacks, rope, and eco-composites, establishing a secure income stream for local farmers. Long-term project plans include continuous water testing to protect the Jimi Dam, as well as ongoing tracking of soil, vegetation, biodiversity, and community health outcomes. Organizers intend for the Jimi pilot to serve as a national model to rehabilitate other mining-damaged land and water systems across Ghana.

items.title: Poor Ghanaians are being jailed because they cannot afford justice – Crime Check Foundation
items.description: The Executive Director of the Crime Check Foundation, Ibrahim Oppong Kwarteng, has criticised Ghana’s justice system, arguing that poverty is contributing to the imprisonment of people who cannot afford fines or adequate legal representation. “What we see at times is not justice. What we see is poverty on trial,” he said, recounting cases encountered by his organisation during more than a decade of work in Ghana’s prisons. Mr Kwarteng made the remarks at an event following a tour of prison establishments across the country, where he highlighted cases he believes expose inequalities in access to justice. “For over 10 years, Crime Check Foundation has worked in Ghana’s 49 prison establishments. And what we see at times is not justice. What we see is poverty on trial,” he said. Mr Kwarteng cited the case of a young mother who, he said, was sentenced to two years in prison after being unable to pay a GH¢300 fine arising from a fight. He also recounted the case of a 19-year-old who was jailed for stealing a bunch of plantain to feed his seven siblings. Another case involved a commercial transport vehicle assistant, commonly known as a trotro mate , who Mr Kwarteng said was imprisoned because he could not afford a lawyer to defend him. “Their crime at times is not stealing. Their crime perhaps is being poor,” he said. The cases, he argued, raise questions about whether people’s financial circumstances are determining how they experience the criminal justice system. Mr Kwarteng also questioned how the justice system could adequately serve poor communities when many people struggle to afford transportation to court or secure legal representation. “Distinguished guests, how can justice be at their doorstep when they cannot afford the transport to the court? And how can justice be at their doorstep when legal aid has less than 40 lawyers across the country?” he asked. He further raised concerns about people spending extended periods on remand without legal representation. “I stand to be corrected. How can justice be at their doorstep when a petty offender spends three years on remand for a case that would have attracted six months if he had a lawyer?” he said. His comments come amid calls for increased resources for the Legal Aid Commission, which provides legal advice and representation to people who cannot afford private legal services. The Commission’s Board Chairman, Supreme Court Justice Samuel Kwame Asiedu Adibu, recently disclosed that it operates 45 offices across Ghana’s 261 districts, with a total staff strength of 190. He said the Commission needed about 180 additional staff to improve its reach. Calls for broader reform The Crime Check Foundation has worked in Ghana’s prisons for more than a decade, supporting inmates, helping secure releases through the payment of fines and advocating for prison reform. The organisation has also raised concerns about the difficulties former prisoners face after their release, including social rejection and barriers to reintegration. Mr Kwarteng’s remarks add to wider concerns about whether poverty, inadequate legal representation and delays in court proceedings are undermining fair access to justice. Addressing those challenges would require stronger legal aid services and closer attention to the circumstances of people held in custody, particularly those unable to afford lawyers or meet court-imposed financial obligations. His account puts the focus on a broader question for Ghana’s justice system: whether a person’s ability to pay should determine how quickly they regain their freedom or how effectively they can defend themselves in court.

items.title: No conflict in appointing Emelia Agbenyo as Deputy EC Chair – NDC
items.description: The Deputy National Director of Elections and IT of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Rashid Tanko-Computer, has dismissed concerns about a potential conflict of interest in the appointment of former party spokesperson Emelia Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC). Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Monday, October 12, he said the appointment should not be considered problematic, citing what he described as similar appointments made under the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) government. He insisted Madam Agbenyo is qualified to fill that position. “There’s no conflict of interest here. I mean, let’s be frank with ourselves,” he said. Mr Tanko-Computer said the NDC had raised concerns about the appointment of individuals with perceived links to the NPP to positions at the EC under former President Nana Akufo-Addo. He cited the appointment of Dr Bossman Asare as a Deputy EC Chairperson, arguing that the NDC had objected to the appointment because of his links to the NPP. According to him, the party had taken its concerns to the Council of State, presenting evidence of what it considered to be the appointees’ political affiliations. However, he said the then Council of State maintained that the individuals were qualified for their positions and that their political affiliations were immaterial. Mr Tanko-Computer said the NDC’s concerns at the time were not heeded, adding that the party’s position on the current appointment should be considered in that context. His response follows cocerns over Ms Agbenyo’s appointment as a Deputy Chairperson of the EC followig her previous role as a governance sector spokesperson for the NDC during the party’s 2024 manifesto process and whether that political association could affect perceptions of the EC’s independence.

items.title: Des supermarchés français touchés par une cyberattaque inédite de leurs installations frigorifiques
items.description: Pas de données volées, mais des produits frais à jeter : plusieurs enseignes de supermarchés françaises ont été victimes dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi d'une cyberattaque « inédite » visant leurs installations frigorifiques, suscitant des craintes en matière de sécurité alimentaire. Au moins 300 points de vente Intermarché/Netto, moins d'une centaine du réseau de Coopérative U, « plusieurs magasins » du groupement E.Leclerc, 80 supermarchés Carrefour et une trentaine de Monoprix sont concernés par cette attaque révélée par BFMTV, ont confirmé à l'AFP ces distributeurs. Sollicité par l'AFP, le parquet de Paris a annoncé le lancement d'une enquête de sa propre initiative sur « la cyberattaque d'ampleur touchant les réfrigérateurs connectés de plusieurs grands magasins ». L'enquête, dirigée par la section anticybercriminalité et « confiée à l'office anticybercriminalité (OFAC), doit permettre de recenser les victimes et d'établir le lien avec les dégâts rapportés » en matière de « pertes de denrées alimentaires » et d'équipements ayant commencé à prendre feu, a-t-il précisé. Selon une source proche du dossier, les systèmes de régulation frigorifique du fabricant danois Danfoss étaient ciblés. L'entreprise scandinave a expliqué à l'AFP que « la majorité des unités touchées sont des produits anciens (…) qui ont atteint leur fin de vie et ne bénéficient plus de mises à jour logicielles ou de sécurité ». Danfoss souligne « recommander depuis longtemps à ses clients de maintenir les systèmes pris en charge à jour et de migrer les systèmes hérités vers des solutions de génération actuelle ». La Fédération du commerce et de la distribution (FCD) a appelé dans un communiqué Danfoss et ses clients frigoristes « à une transparence totale sur la situation et à la mise en œuvre sans délai de toutes les mesures nécessaires ». Les pirates ont réussi, à distance, « à mettre en dégivrage tous nos meubles froids et à les monter en température jusqu'à 50 degrés », a expliqué le patron des Mousquetaires/Intermarché, Thierry Cotillard, lundi soir sur BFMTV. « Ca va être des dizaines de millions d'euros au niveau national en une seule matinée de gestion de crise » , c'est du « jamais vu » , a-t-il chiffré, évoquant « un vrai sujet de vulnérabilité » concernant « notre souveraineté alimentaire ». Selon Intermarché, les distributeurs sont contraints de « jeter l'ensemble des produits » touchés pour respecter la chaîne du froid, estimant que « l'un des points durs » aura trait aux assurances qui ne « couvrent pas ce type » d'incident. « S'attaquer à des équipements essentiels à la conservation des produits frais et à l'approvisionnement alimentaire des Français est d'une extrême gravité et est inédit », a réagi le PDG de Coopérative U, Dominique Schelcher, sur X. E. Leclerc a également évoqué à l'AFP « une attaque informatique » ayant « affecté l'un de ses fournisseurs de matériel frigorifique ». D'après l'entourage du Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu a « immédiatement demandé à l'Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (Anssi) de se saisir du sujet » et « suit le dossier personnellement ». L'Anssi a confirmé être « mobilisée », tant « à l'échelon français pour accompagner les potentielles victimes, qu'à l'échelon européen pour se coordonner avec ses homologues ». De son côté, le ministère du Commerce assure être « en lien avec les distributeurs ». Longtemps isolés d'internet, les équipements industriels comme les groupes frigorifiques sont désormais connectés via des capteurs ou des systèmes de supervision à distance, explique à l'AFP Antoine Hautin, secrétaire général d'Almond, cabinet de conseil en cybersécurité. « Historiquement, ces systèmes ont été conçus pour privilégier la fiabilité et la maîtrise des coûts, plutôt que la protection contre les cyberattaques » car « les attaquants ne pouvaient pas y accéder à distance », souligne l'expert. Selon lui, en touchant vraisemblablement des centaines d'équipements simultanément, l'attaque de lundi témoigne d'une « une certaine sophistication ». Danfoss avait fait part ces derniers mois de plusieurs vulnérabilités graves sur certains de ses logiciels utilisés dans les systèmes frigorifiques. Le 18 septembre, le fabricant avait évoqué une faille permettant « à des attaquants d'obtenir un accès en lecture et en écriture aux valeurs internes, de télécharger et d'exécuter » des programmes informatiques non sécurisés. The post Des supermarchés français touchés par une cyberattaque inédite de leurs installations frigorifiques appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 87-year-old man jailed 20 years for defiling 9-year-old girl at Ofankor
items.description: An 87-year-old man, Yaw Gahornu, has been sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with hard labour for defiling a nine-year-old girl at Ofankor, a suburb of Accra. The sentence was secured by the Tesano Divisional Police Command following investigations into the case, according to a statement issued by the Accra Regional Police Command on October 12, 2026. The Police said preliminary investigations indicated that on August 29, 2026, the girl’s mother returned from work and noticed bloodstains on her daughter’s clothing. When questioned, the child disclosed that Mr Gahornu had allegedly subjected her to repeated sexual abuse between July and August 2026. Further investigations indicated that the accused allegedly lured the girl to his sleeping quarters and threatened to kill her if she reported the abuse to her mother. The Police said the alleged abuse was witnessed by the accused’s granddaughter on August 31, 2026. She subsequently informed family members, including the girl’s mother, leading to a report to the Police. Mr Gahornu was charged and arraigned before the Gender-Based Violence Court at the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) Headquarters, where he was found guilty and sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with hard labour for defilement. The Accra Regional Police Command welcomed the outcome of the case and reaffirmed its commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons. It urged the public to promptly report suspected cases of child abuse to the Police for investigation and appropriate action.

items.title: Houthi official warns of ‘swift, painful response’ if US enters Yemen war
items.description: A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a “painful response” if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington’s help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks. Yemen’s civil war — in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis — reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis. The Houthis quickly began targeting Saudi oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs, including with a string of lethal strikes on Riyadh’s airport, rocking the world’s top oil exporter. Blasts resounded over the capital again on Monday night, with the Saudi coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile. Following an attack Saturday at the airport that killed 13 people, US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom. “If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told AFP in an interview. He also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”. Saturday’s strike on King Khalid International Airport was the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, and also left hundreds wounded. Trump said the attack was “not acceptable” and that he would be speaking to the kingdom’s de facto leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, telling reporters the US was “going to look at” the possibility of joining Saudi strikes. Four people died in earlier strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh’s outskirts on Monday. – ‘Serious’ response – Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”. Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told a conference in Riyadh on Monday that the recent events had “tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience”. “The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.” CCTV footage of Saturday’s attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden blast tore through the building and brought down flaming debris. The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats. In the evening, mobile phones received a loud government alert warning of a “hostile aerial threat” before the announcement of the interception. It was the first use of the phone alert system in Riyadh in weeks, with no official reason given for the lack of messaging during the attacks targeting the capital in recent days. – Flights suspended – The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said US government employees must obtain its authorisation before using any airport in the kingdom, and urged US citizens to “take extreme caution” if they chose to do so. The mission also said “American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events” in Saudi Arabia. The UAE’s national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week, and also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah. Bahrain’s national carrier Gulf Air said it too was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday. US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh, scheduled for October 23. Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences. Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University, said that despite some success, “Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves”. Riyadh leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa. Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”. The long-running Yemeni civil war has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country. UN rights chief Volker Turk said he was “appalled by the repeated attacks” on Saudi Arabia, but urged both sides to back down, adding “continued fighting will only unleash further misery with no end in sight”. items.title: Petrol price down by Rs2.93 per litre, high-speed diesel rate up by Re0.61
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Monday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2.93 per litre, but increased that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.61 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs395.37 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.85 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 13 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Sankofa Gold targets 70kg output after 9-month shutdown
items.description: Prestea Sankofa Gold Limited is targeting 70 kilogrammes of gold production by the end of October 2026 following a nine-month shutdown, as the state-owned company works to restore operations and improve processing efficiency. The company has resumed production, with a target of processing 850 tonnes of material daily, according to Senior Plant Manager for Processing, Reginald Soweh. “We are looking at production of 850 tons per day, by which we expect to make a target of 70 kilograms of gold at the end of the month,” he said. Management is also seeking to improve gold recovery rates from about 75 per cent previously to 80.0%, with a longer-term target of exceeding 90.0%. The resumption follows months of inactivity during which the company undertook maintenance works on its processing plant and addressed concerns over the capacity of its existing tailings dam. New tailings dam critical to sustained production The company is constructing a second tailings dam to receive waste generated during gold processing. According to the company’s Public Relations Officer, Ebenezer Essien, the shutdown was partly necessitated by the need to maintain the existing facility, which was approaching capacity, while undertaking repairs and maintenance on the processing plant. The existing dam requires careful monitoring because waste from gold processing contains chemicals that could pose risks to the environment if improperly contained. Mr Essien said the Environmental Protection Authority and the Minerals Commission had engaged the company over the facility and granted it approximately three months to continue depositing waste in the existing dam while work on the replacement facility is completed. Management says the new dam is about 80 per cent complete. The Managing Director of Prestea Sankofa Gold Limited, Alhaji Ishaq Dauda, said the project was estimated to cost US$5 million and was being financed internally. “The dam is approximately five million dollars, and we are funding it internally,” he said. A company press release dated October 7, 2026, indicated that construction was expected to be completed by the end of November, subject to the successful completion of the remaining works. The completion of the facility is expected to support continued operations, although its readiness to receive processing waste will be important in determining whether production can proceed without interruption. Financial pressure and employment prospects The prolonged shutdown also raised concerns about the company’s ability to meet its financial obligations without generating income from production. The Western Regional Minister Joseph Nelson, who visited the facility with the Member of Parliament for Prestea Huni-Valley, Wisdom Cudjoe, and the Municipal Chief Executive, Dr Mathew Ayeh, said the shutdown had been a concern because the company still had obligations to meet. “For any company, it’s not healthy. I mean, you are not generating any income, and yet the company is expected to, you know, look after its staff and all other obligations that will require funds,” he said. Mr Essien, however, said workers continued to receive their salaries during the period when production was suspended, with no salary arrears arising from the shutdown, according to management. The company also says it has engaged about 150 young people from surrounding communities as graduate trainees and casual workers. Management expects further expansion to create additional employment opportunities. The Regional Minister has urged management to sustain the recovery and ensure that the company’s operations translate into employment and wider economic benefits for Prestea and surrounding communities. The immediate test for Prestea Sankofa Gold Limited will be whether it can meet its production target, complete the new tailings dam and maintain uninterrupted operations. The company has not yet provided a verified figure for the financial cost of the nine-month shutdown.

items.title: Moulay El Hassan préside l'ouverture du 17è Salon du Cheval d'El Jadida
items.description: Le Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan a présidé, lundi au Parc d’expositions Mohammed VI d'El Jadida, la cérémonie d'ouverture de la 17e édition du Salon du Cheval d'El Jadida, organisée sous le haut patronage du Roi Mohammed VI, sous le thème « Le cheval au service de l'humain ». L'ouverture par le Prince Héritier de ce Salon, qui se poursuit jusqu’au 18 octobre, traduit la Haute Sollicitude dont le Roi Mohammed VI n’a eu de cesse d'entourer le secteur équestre et la ferme volonté du Souverain de structurer durablement cette filière, de l'élevage jusqu’aux compétitions internationales, et d'en promouvoir le rayonnement à l'international. À son arrivée au Parc d'expositions, Moulay El Hassan a été accueilli par Moulay Abdellah Alaoui, Président de l'Association du Salon du Cheval, avant de passer en revue une section de la Garde Royale qui rendait les honneurs. Il a ensuite été salué par le wali de la région de Casablanca-Settat, le président du Conseil régional, le secrétaire général du département de l'Agriculture au ministère de l'Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime, du Développement rural et des Eaux et Forêts, le gouverneur de la province d'El Jadida, le président du Conseil provincial d'El Jadida, la présidente de la commune de Haouzia, les membres du Conseil d'administration et les sponsors de l'Association du Salon du Cheval, ainsi que par les cadres du ministère. À l'entrée du hall d'exposition, le Prince Héritier a été salué par les invités d'honneur de cette 17e édition, notamment Mustafa Ilker Kilic, ambassadeur de la République de Turkiye au Maroc, Khalid Salim Ahmed Bamakhalif, ambassadeur du Sultanat d'Oman au Maroc, Omar Al Tunaiji, chargé d'affaires à l'ambassade des Émirats Arabes Unis, Mohamed Ahmed Al Harbi, directeur général de l'Association des chevaux pur-sang arabes des Émirats Arabes Unis, Rashed Al Kaabi, du bureau de la Présidence des Émirats Arabes Unis, le colonel d'État-Major Ahmed Bin Khalfan Al Lamki, directeur général par intérim de la Cavalerie Royale du Sultanat d'Oman et Obaid Khalfan Al Mazrouei, Président de l’Autorité du Patrimoine d’Abou Dhabi. Moulay El Hassan a, par la suite, visité les différents stands du Salon, dédiés aux institutionnels, aux éleveurs, à l'artisanat, à l'international, à l'art et culture, aux régions du Royaume et aux sponsors, ainsi que le village des enfants « Faris en voyage à travers le Maroc » , un espace immersif destiné à faire découvrir au jeune public le riche patrimoine équestre du Royaume. Il a ensuite assisté, à la carrière principale, à des shows, des spectacles artistiques et des voltiges équestres exécutés par des troupes et cavaliers marocains et étrangers, avant de se diriger vers l’espace de la Tbourida où Il a suivi des spectacles de fantasia animés par 18 Sorbas représentant les différentes régions du Royaume. Rendez-vous incontournable de cette 17e édition du Salon, le Grand Prix du Roi Mohammed VI de Tbourida met à l’honneur l’une des plus prestigieuses traditions équestres du Maroc, une discipline qui conjugue la maîtrise du cheval, la parfaite coordination des cavaliers et le respect de traditions séculaires. Inscrite en 2021 sur la Liste représentative du patrimoine culturel immatériel de l’Humanité de l’UNESCO, la Tbourida, véritable expression de l’identité culturelle marocaine, incarne un héritage vivant transmis de génération en génération. À cette occasion, le Prince Héritier a posé pour une photo souvenir avec les Moqaddems des 18 Sorbas. Initié par l'Association du Salon du Cheval, le Salon du Cheval d'El Jadida, qui a acquis une renommée nationale et internationale sans cesse grandissante, propose une programmation scientifique, culturelle et ludique riche et diversifiée. Ainsi, plusieurs activités liées au cheval y sont organisées dans le cadre de compétitions ou exhibitions de haut niveau. L'édition 2026 marque une étape importante dans le positionnement international du Salon dans la mesure où le Grand Prix Roi Mohammed VI de Saut d'Obstacles franchit un nouveau cap avec son passage au niveau CSI 5*-W. Les volets culturel et scientifique ne sont pas en reste, le cheval étant au centre de nombreuses conférences, ateliers et tables rondes, ainsi que de multiples activités ludiques réservées au jeune public. items.title: Tamale, Bolgatanga had just one Legal Aid lawyer between them – Kwesimintsim MP
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Kwesimintsim, Philip Fiifi Buckman, has described Legal Aid Commission services in northern Ghana as “pathetic”, saying Tamale and Bolgatanga had only one lawyer serving the Commission between them. Mr Buckman, a member of Parliament’s Constitutional and Legal Affairs Committee, made the remarks at the launch of the 2026 Legal Aid Week in Accra, recounting a recent oversight visit to the northern regions. “We went to Bolgatanga and Tamale, and it was pathetic. The whole of Bolgatanga, the whole of Tamale had only one lawyer for the Legal Aid Commission. The whole of Tamale,” he said. He said the committee was told that the same lawyer was responsible for both cities, highlighting what he described as a serious shortage of legal personnel available to support people who cannot afford legal representation. “In fact, we are even happy, or we were happy to hear that the person who was in charge of Bolgatanga was the same person in charge of Tamale,” he added. Mr Buckman urged the government to take decisive steps to provide the Commission with the resources it needs to fulfil its mandate. “We as a government, I say we as a government because I’m part of government, have to take the bold decision to resource the Legal Aid Commission enough to perform its duties,” he said. His comments follow an appeal by the Commission’s Board Chairman, Supreme Court Justice Samuel Kwame Asiedu Adibu, for urgent support to address staffing and office shortages. Justice Adibu said the Commission has 190 staff nationwide and operates 45 offices across Ghana’s 261 districts. It has a presence in only 10 of the country’s 16 regions. He also disclosed that the Commission was short by about 180 staff, limiting its ability to reach people who need legal services. The Legal Aid Commission is mandated under the Legal Aid Commission Act, 2018 (Act 977), to provide legal assistance to indigent and vulnerable people. Sections 24 and 25 of the Act provide for the establishment of offices in every region and district, but the Commission’s current reach falls short of that requirement. The staffing and infrastructure gaps raise concerns about the ability of people in underserved communities to obtain legal advice and representation when dealing with courts, police and other parts of the justice system. The Commission has repeatedly called for increased financial, infrastructural and human resource support to expand its services. Mr Buckman’s remarks add to calls for the government to address the shortfall, with the scale of the resources committed likely to shape how effectively the Commission can extend legal aid to underserved communities.

items.title: PAC orders eviction of former irrigation company MD from official residence
items.description: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has directed the Ministry of Food and Agriculture to involve the police to remove the former Managing Director of an irrigation company in the Upper East Region from an official residence if he fails to vacate the property. The directive follows a prolonged dispute over the continued occupation of the facility by Dr Benedict Bonaventure Aligebam after his tenure as Managing Director ended. The situation has reportedly created operational challenges for the company, with the current Managing Director, Dr Dominic Anarigide, residing in Bolgatanga while working at Navrongo. Dr Anarigide told the Committee that efforts to resolve the matter had so far proved unsuccessful, despite interventions by the former Chief of Staff and other officials. The dispute centres on a decision by the company’s former board to extend Dr Aligebam’s contract for two years, which was subsequently revised to three months. The disagreement led to legal action after the former Managing Director was locked out of his office. Records presented indicate that a court dismissed an injunction application he filed in connection with the matter. However, Dr Aligebam has continued to occupy the official residence, reportedly arguing that his belongings remain in the office and that he was unlawfully locked out. The issue came before the PAC as it examined findings in the Auditor-General’s Report on the company, which has also been linked to financial irregularities and other administrative challenges. The Committee consequently directed the Ministry to seek police assistance to ensure the former Managing Director vacates the residence should he fail to do so voluntarily.

items.title: Rentrée scolaire 2026-2027: plus de 4 millions d’élèves à l’école aujourd’hui
items.description: Après un report dû aux conséquences des pluies diluviennes survenues récemment au Sénégal, la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 s'est tenue ce lundi 12 octobre sur l’étendue du territoire national. Cette année, plus de 4 millions de potaches répartis entre le préscolaire, l’élémentaire et le moyen secondaire sont attendus. L’État, comme à l’accoutumée, a déjà pris les devants en accélérant le programme de construction de 2.500 classes et d’ouvrages annexes ainsi que le recrutement en urgence de 2.527 enseignants qui viendront s’ajouter aux sortants des centres régionaux de formation et de la Fastef. L’école sénégalaise rouvre à nouveau ses portes ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, après un report le 8 octobre dernier dû aux fortes pluies. Cette année, selon les chiffres rendus publics lors du Conseil interministériel tenu par le gouvernement le 25 septembre dernier sur le sujet, plus de 4 millions d’élèves sont attendus dans les classes du préscolaire, de l’élémentaire et du moyen secondaire. Le gouvernement est en train d’accélérer aussi l’exécution du programme de construction de 2.500 classes et d’ouvrages annexes et de veiller au respect du calendrier contractuel de livraison, dans le cadre des mesures arrêtées lors du Conseil interministériel consacré à la préparation de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027. Au total, 27 mesures ont été retenues à l’issue de cette rencontre présidée par le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou M. Lô, avait annoncé le ministre, secrétaire général du gouvernement, Papa Assane Touré. Parmi ces décisions, le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Moustapha Guirassy, en relation avec ses homologues chargés des Infrastructures et de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan, avait été invité à accélérer la mise en œuvre du programme de construction de 2.500 classes et ouvrages annexes. « Cette mesure vise à permettre un démarrage effectif des enseignements dans des établissements offrant des conditions d’accueil adaptées aux élèves et apprenants », renseignait le communiqué publié au terme de la rencontre gouvernementale. Celui-ci revenait aussi sur l’engagement du gouvernement à lutter contre le déficit d’enseignants dans le système. Cette année, outre les sortants de la Faculté des sciences et technologies de l'éducation et de la formation (Fastef) et des centres régionaux de formation de personnels enseignants, l’État a procédé au recrutement spécial de 2.527 enseignants. Il a été aussi retenu la construction ou la réhabilitation et l’équipement de 50 cases des tout-petits et de certaines structures de développement intégré de la petite enfance. Ces différentes mesures s’inscrivent dans la volonté du gouvernement de garantir la fonctionnalité des structures éducatives dès le début de l’année scolaire 2026-2027. Pour voir ce que cela va donner de manière concrète sur le terrain, le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Moustapha Guirassy, effectuera la traditionnelle tournée de supervision de la rentrée dans certains établissements. Cette année, il a jeté le dévolu dans la banlieue dakaroise où des écoles sont encore fortement impactées par les récentes pluies. M. Guirassy conduira tour à tour une délégation au Complexe Seydina Issa Laye de Cambérène et au Groupe scolaire Elimane Ndiaye de l’académie de Pikine-Guédiawaye. Seydou Prosper SADIO

items.title: Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway progressing as planned – FG
items.description: The Federal Government says construction of the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is progressing as planned, dismissing reports that the project had been abandoned for the East-West Road. Sen.​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‍⁠​​‍‌​ David Umahi, Minister of Works, stated this while briefing newsmen on Monday at the State House in Abuja. Umahi said construction is ongoing along various sections of the highway, adding that the project remained intact and was being implemented as designed. “The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is moving and moving even faster than envisaged. Don’t forget that Section One, covering 147.47 kilometres, is being fully constructed in Lagos,” he said. The minister said Section Two, covering 55 kilometres, was expected to be ready by mid-November. He said work is ongoing on Sections Three A and Three B, covering about 75 kilometres in Akwa Ibom and Cross River states, with progress exceeding 40 per cent. Umahi added that construction is ongoing on Sections Four A and Four B, covering 65 kilometres across Ogun and Ondo states. He said work had also commenced on Section Five, covering 62.5 kilometres in Akwa Ibom, with more than 20 per cent progress recorded within less than three months. The minister explained that the ministry is seeking President Bola Tinubu’s approval to incorporate about 400 kilometres of the East-West Road into the ongoing infrastructure development programme. He said the proposed intervention would cover sections linking Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom and Cross River states. Umahi said the East-West Road required attention because some sections had suffered damage from flooding, citing affected portions in Delta and Edo. He stressed that the proposed work on the East-West Road would complement, rather than replace, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. “Nobody has abandoned the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. We have designers and surveyors working along the route, including in Edo, Delta, Bayelsa and Rivers,” he said. Umahi said the Federal Government is undertaking surveys along the route to ensure the project’s continued development and integration with other infrastructure projects in the Niger Delta. He added that the highway remained part of the Federal Government’s legacy infrastructure projects and that its alignment would not be altered. “The 750-kilometre coastal highway is intact and cannot be changed. Nobody has the power to change it because it is already designed and ongoing,” he said. (NAN) The post Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway progressing as planned – FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Legal Aid Commission has offices in only 45 of Ghana’s 261 districts, needs 180 more staff
items.description: The Legal Aid Commission is appealing for urgent support to address staff shortages and limited office coverage that are restricting access to legal services for vulnerable Ghanaians. The Commission’s Board Chairman and Supreme Court Judge, Justice Samuel Kwame Asiedu Adibu, disclosed the challenges at the launch of the 2026 Legal Aid Week in Accra. He said the Commission has a total staff strength of 190 and operates 45 offices across the country’s 261 districts, leaving much of the population without a nearby office to access its services. Under Sections 24 and 25 of the Legal Aid Commission Act, 2018 (Act 977), the Commission is required to establish offices in every region and district. However, Justice Adibu said it currently has offices in only 10 of Ghana’s 16 regions and 45 of the 261 districts. “We are short by about 180 staff,” he said, adding that the shortfall limits the Commission’s ability to reach people who need legal assistance. “It is therefore obvious that a significant proportion of those who may be in need of legal services and assistance are not accessible to the Commission,” he said. Justice Adibu warned that the absence of legal aid services in many communities could prevent poor and vulnerable people from effectively engaging with the justice system. “While there may be courts and police stations in many parts of the country, access to a lawyer or paralegal may be non-existent to facilitate meaningful engagement with the justice system by an indigent or vulnerable person,” he said. The Commission provides legal advice, representation and other assistance to people who cannot afford legal services. Its mandate also includes public education on legal rights and supporting the realisation of constitutional rights. However, inadequate funding, limited infrastructure and a shortage of legal personnel continue to constrain its operations. The launch of Legal Aid Week is intended to raise awareness of the Commission’s work and draw attention to the resources needed to expand access to justice. The Commission has previously called for increased financial, infrastructural and human resource support. It has also announced initiatives, including a 24-hour call centre, to improve access to services such as Alternative Dispute Resolution. Justice Adibu, who was sworn in as Board Chairman in January 2026, is expected to help steer the development of a comprehensive legal aid policy and programme for nationwide implementation. The latest appeal highlights the gap between the Commission’s statutory responsibilities and its current operational reach, with most districts lacking a dedicated Legal Aid Commission office.

items.title: Vénus Findy Touré, entrepreneure: l’élégance et l’originalité en viatique
items.description: Vénus Findy Touré s’est forgée un parcours professionnel riche et diversifié, marqué par la formation, la persévérance et le sens de l’engagement. Cadre, entrepreneure et passionnée de mode, elle a construit sa trajectoire entre art, études et responsabilités professionnelles, avec la confiance en soi et le goût de l’effort comme principaux repères. « Dagay wolou sa bop », aime-t-elle répéter. En wolof, s’aimer soi-même, ou encore avoir confiance en soi. Pour Vénus Findy Touré, cette expression résume une philosophie de vie forgée dès l’enfance et qui continue de guider ses choix. À l’écouter raconter son parcours, l’on devine que la réussite ne se décrète pas. Elle se construit dans l’effort, l’éducation et la capacité à croire en soi. Son prénom, Vénus, porte déjà une histoire. Son père, Mamadou Kémadou Touré, l’a choisi en référence à la déesse de la beauté et à un passage évoqué par l’écrivain Birago Diop dans un de ses poèmes. « Il disait qu’on lui avait amené une Vénus », raconte-t-elle. Findy, son deuxième prénom, est celui de sa grand-mère paternelle. Aînée d’une fratrie de quatre enfants, elle grandit à la Médina avant de rejoindre Keur Massar après le déménagement de sa famille. Il faut le dire, l’enfance de Findy est profondément marquée par l’art. Son papa, poète et écrivain, nourrit le rêve de voir sa fille devenir artiste. Et pour lui forger une assurance à toute épreuve et dépasser la peur du public, son paternel l’inscrit très tôt à l’École nationale des Arts. Vénus y apprend le piano pendant sept ans et se familiarise avec la scène. Les examens et prestations au Théâtre national Daniel Sorano lui apprennent à affronter le public sans trac. « On nous apprenait à balayer la salle du regard sans jamais nous laisser déstabiliser », se souvient-elle. De cette formation artistique précoce, elle garde une aisance oratoire remarquable et une absence totale de complexe face aux défis. Forgée par la famille et l’art Dans cet élan, après son cursus scolaire au lycée Lamine Guèye, Vénus construit son parcours académique et professionnel à force de détermination, payant elle-même ses études supérieures pour obtenir ses diplômes. Grâce à la « Baraka » qu’elle dit rechercher dans toute chose, son entrée dans le monde professionnel intervient tôt. Elle travaille notamment dans une agence de voyages avant de passer cinq années à l’hôtel Radisson de Dakar (Ndlr : actuel Hôtel Noom), où elle se spécialise dans l’organisation de séminaires et d’événements. C’est dans cet environnement qu’elle est remarquée pour ses qualités professionnelles et son sens du service. Une rencontre va alors changer la trajectoire de sa carrière. Elle rejoint l’Artp, où elle évolue depuis une douzaine d’années. Aujourd’hui, assistante du président du Collège de l’organisme de régulation, elle évolue au cœur des dossiers stratégiques avec un professionnalisme irréprochable. Entrepreneure Mais réduire Vénus Touré à son activité professionnelle serait méconnaître une personnalité aux multiples facettes. En 2014, elle crée « Vénus Univers », une marque africaine de vêtements. Des pièces confectionnées au Sénégal sont proposées à une clientèle au-delà des frontières, notamment à travers des ventes privées à Abidjan et au Canada. La marque revendique une identité « Made in Africa », avec également des collaborations avec des tailleurs établis en Côte d’Ivoire. La mode, à vrai dire, n’est pas étrangère à l’histoire de l’entrepreneure. Plus jeune, elle a défilé et participé à différents concours. La musique, elle aussi, demeure présente. « J’adore la musique », confie-t-elle. Deux univers qui prolongent, à leur manière, l’éducation artistique reçue. Défenseuse de l’originalité Avec la confiance et son sens des responsabilités acquis très tôt, Vénus nourrit aujourd’hui un discours sur la dépigmentation. Selon elle, la beauté d’une personne ne saurait être appréciée uniquement à l’aune de la couleur de sa peau. C’est ainsi qu’elle assume son teint naturel et encourage les femmes à prendre soin de leur peau sans chercher à la modifier artificiellement. « La vraie beauté, c’est la confiance en soi », martèle-t-elle. Pour elle, la pression sociale, le regard du conjoint, des proches ou encore l’image véhiculée par certaines séries télévisées peuvent alimenter les complexes. Elle insiste surtout sur le rôle des parents. Il faut, selon elle, apprendre très tôt aux enfants à s’aimer et à valoriser leurs qualités plutôt que leurs supposés défauts. À 45 ans, mère accomplie de deux garçons qu’elle a élevés avec le sens de l’effort et de la dignité, Vénus Findy Touré continue d’avancer, guidée par le goût de l’effort et le sens des sacrifices. « Dans la vie, le repos n’est pas une option tant qu’il reste du savoir à acquérir et des projets à bâtir », insiste-t-elle. Une femme de tête et de cœur, inspirante, qui laisse forcément une empreinte positive dans le cœur et l’esprit de toute personne qu’elle rencontre. Par Souleymane WANE

items.title: Tinubu’s N60 fuel discount was a ‘stunt’ — Makinde campaign
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of using its N60 per litre petrol discount as a political stunt to deflect public anger rather than ease Nigerians’ economic hardship. The campaign organisation said the reported increase in petrol prices from N1,370 to N1,410 per litre at filling stations in Abuja and other parts of the country had reinforced its earlier warning that the discount was no solution to the rising cost of living. In a statement by its Director of Communications, Richard Ihediwa, the organisation accused the administration of using propaganda to project an image of compassion while Nigerians continued to bear the burden of economic hardship. “The latest development also strengthens our position that no amount of propaganda can conceal the consequences of policies, whose promised benefits are not reflected in the daily lives of ordinary Nigerians,” it said. The organisation also faulted the government’s economic reform narrative, arguing that the promise of bold reforms had become an excuse for imposing greater hardship on citizens. “Nigerians cannot continue to be confronted with the hollow slogan of ‘bold economic reforms,’ which has become a euphemism for transferring the crushing burden of economic hardship onto citizens already struggling to survive,” the campaign organisation said. It called for a fundamental rethink of the policies driving the hardship, warning that temporary concessions would remain inadequate without changes to the country’s economic direction. Turning its criticism into a political argument, the organisation presented the Makinde/Daura ticket as an alternative to the Tinubu administration, citing its RESET NIGERIA Agenda, which it said was anchored on responsible economic management, transparent resource governance and productive investment. “Nigeria needs a complete RESET under a Makinde Presidency and not this propaganda-driven administration that have failed in all ramifications,” Ihediwa said. The post Tinubu’s N60 fuel discount was a ‘stunt’ — Makinde campaign appeared first on Vanguard News .
